summary: Defines two RTCP Extended Report blocks for reporting concealment metrics for audio applications of RTP, which describe how often lost audio was covered up.

eli5.summary: When a piece of a phone call is lost, software fills the gap to make it less bumpy. These reports tell how much of that filling was done.

questions: what is a severely concealed second
what is packet loss concealment in rtp
subtitle: Two RTCP report blocks that tell a sender how much of an audio call the receiver had to patch over.

tldr.problem: When audio packets are lost or arrive late, receivers cover the gaps with locally generated sound, but the sender has no standard way to learn how much of this happened.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7294 defines the Loss Concealment Metrics Block (type 30) and the Concealed Seconds Metrics Block (type 31) as RTCP Extended Report blocks, and an SDP syntax to signal them.
tldr.outcome: Endpoints and monitors can see how long playout was normal versus concealed, and how many whole seconds were impaired.

today: RFC 7294 is a Proposed Standard published in July 2014, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Normal and Concealed Playout
sections.content:
At any instant, a receiver's audio output is either normal or concealed. Normal means playing audio received from the remote end, and also locally generated signals such as announcements, tones and comfort noise. Concealed means playing locally generated signals that mask network impairments or reduce the audibility of jitter buffer adaptations.

RFC 7294 defines two new RTCP Extended Report (XR) block types, building on the packet loss concealment mechanism in Section 4.7.6 of RFC 3611. They apply to audio applications of RTP, and to the audio part of audio/video applications where the concealment machinery sits at the receiving end. The blocks MUST be used as defined in RFC 3550 and RFC 3611.
sections.eli5: If a word is missing from a song on the radio, someone quietly hums to cover the gap. This RFC is about counting how much humming was needed.

sections.title: The Loss Concealment Metrics Block
sections.content:
Block type 30 reports how the receiver handled packet loss and discard. Its block length is 6. It carries three durations measured in units of RTP timestamp: On-Time Playout Duration (normal playout, including both speech and silence), Loss Concealment Duration (playout of substitute audio because a frame was not present when needed), and Buffer Adjustment Concealment Duration (controlled insertion or deletion of samples from jitter buffer adaptation). Two more fields give the Playout Interrupt Count and the Mean Playout Interrupt Size.

Loss and buffer-adjustment concealment are separate because buffer adjustment is typically arranged in silence periods and is usually less audible. Concealment that cannot be classed as buffer adjustment MUST be classed as loss.

The 2-bit I field says whether values are interval (10) or cumulative (11). Senders MUST NOT use 00 or 01, and receivers MUST discard such blocks. The 2-bit plc field names the concealment method in use: 0 silence insertion, 1 simple replay with no attenuation, 2 simple replay with attenuation, 3 enhancement. Reserved bits MUST be zero. For the 32-bit durations, 0xFFFFFFFE means out of range and 0xFFFFFFFF means unavailable.

The block relies on a Measurement Information Block from RFC 6776 to describe the measurement period. It SHOULD be sent in the same compound RTCP packet, and MUST be discarded if that period is not received there.
sections.eli5: This report is a stopwatch summary. It says how long the call sounded real, how long it was patched up, and how many times it broke.

sections.title: The Concealed Seconds Metrics Block
sections.content:
Block type 31, with block length 4, counts whole seconds, in the style of the errored-seconds metric of PSTN T1/E1 lines. Seconds come from successive one-second intervals of an RTP clock that need not match any external time, so they are not necessarily calendar seconds. As a result, two loss events 50 ms apart could count as one Concealed Second or two, depending on where the boundaries fall. At the end of a session, a leftover period over 500 ms is counted and one under 500 ms is disregarded.

  • Unimpaired Seconds: seconds with no frame loss or discard due to late arrival. Comfort noise during talker silence counts as unimpaired.
  • Concealed Seconds: seconds with any frame loss or discard due to late arrival. The count MUST include Severely Concealed Seconds. Buffer adjustment concealment SHOULD NOT be counted, except that it SHOULD be counted when it happens at an inopportune moment such as a large, immediate adaptation during active speech.
  • Severely Concealed Seconds: seconds where the time lost or discarded exceeds the SCS Threshold.

The SCS Threshold is in 0:8 format, so it can represent 0 to 99.6 percent. A default of 5 percent effective frame loss (50 ms per second) is suggested, which is 0x0D. The same I and plc rules as in the first block apply, and the same measurement-period requirement.
sections.eli5: Instead of timing the gaps, this report counts seconds on a clock. A second with a patched-up hole counts as bumpy, and a second with a lot of patching counts as very bumpy.

sections.title: Signaling in SDP
sections.content:
RFC 3611 defines how SDP signals XR blocks, and XR blocks MAY be used without prior signaling. This RFC adds two values of xr-format to the rtcp-xr attribute: loss-conceal for the first block, and conc-sec with an optional =thresh for the second. The thresh is a string of digits, a threshold for SCS in milliseconds.

In offer/answer use, the rules of RFC 3611 apply, and the thresh value is declared by the offer.
sections.eli5: Before the call, each side can say which of these reports it would like to send or receive.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: IANA registered two block types in the RTCP XR Block Type registry: LCB, Loss Concealment Metrics Block, value 30, and CSB, Concealed Seconds Metrics Block, value 31. It also registered the SDP parameters loss-conceal and conc-sec. The registrations list the RAI Area Directors as contact.
sections.eli5: The two new reports were given official numbers, 30 and 31, so everyone uses the same ones.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says it is believed that these blocks introduce no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 3611. They do not provide per-packet statistics, so the confidentiality risk described in Section 7, paragraph 3 of RFC 3611 does not apply.
sections.eli5: The reports only give totals, not details about each packet, so they reveal little.

fields.name: On-Time Playout Duration
fields.desc: Normal playout, in RTP timestamp units.

fields.name: Unimpaired Seconds
fields.desc: Seconds with no frame loss or late discard.

fields.name: Concealed Seconds
fields.desc: Seconds with any frame loss or late discard.

items.label: Simple replay, with attenuation
items.desc: Earlier audio is replayed with attenuation.

items.label: Enhancement
items.desc: Improved quality; equivalent to enhanced in RFC 3611 Section 4.7.6.
